overview: Arch Capital Group Ltd. is a Bermuda-based specialty insurance, reinsurance, and mortgage insurance holding company with roughly $27 billion of capital, operating worldwide through wholly owned subsidiaries. The company underwrites a diversified book across three segments -- Insurance, Reinsurance, and Mortgage -- targeting specialty property, casualty, and mortgage-credit risk rather than broad commodity lines. Arch is known for disciplined, cycle-driven capital allocation, shifting capacity among segments and lines as pricing moves through the underwriting cycle.

business_model.summary: Arch earns underwriting profit (premiums minus losses and expenses) plus investment income on its float across three complementary segments. The Insurance segment (commercial P&C, professional lines, E&S/surplus lines) and Reinsurance segment (property cat, casualty, marine/aviation, specialty treaty reinsurance) are cyclical, priced annually or multi-year; the Mortgage segment (U.S. primary mortgage insurance on GSE loans, plus reinsurance/GSE risk transfer) is longer-duration, high-margin, and less correlated with P&C catastrophe cycles, giving Arch a natural diversification buffer.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - commercial policyholders, mortgage lenders/GSEs, and ceding insurers/reinsurance brokers; no direct retail/consumer distribution
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily U.S. and Bermuda-domiciled risk with global reinsurance clients (North America, Europe, Bermuda, London market, Asia-Pacific); U.S. MidCorp/Entertainment insurance business expanded U.S. middle-market presence in 2024

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-to-large specialty (re)insurer without dominant market share in any single P&C line; top-6 U.S. private mortgage insurer by NIW volume, competing closely with MGIC, Essent, Radian, Enact, and National MI

moat_factors.description: Management has a long track record of shifting capital between Insurance, Reinsurance and Mortgage segments toward whichever offers the best risk-adjusted returns, avoiding chasing soft-market volume
Mortgage credit risk is largely uncorrelated with P&C catastrophe risk, smoothing consolidated combined ratios through the cycle
A+ / A1-range ratings and ~$27B of capital support large-line specialty and reinsurance capacity that smaller peers cannot match
Deep actuarial and underwriting talent in niche E&S, professional lines, and structured reinsurance; MidCorp/Entertainment acquisition adds franchise value in a specialty niche
Limited pricing power versus mega-reinsurers like Berkshire and Munich Re; commercial insurance and reinsurance are largely broker-intermediated and price-competitive

weaknesses: No dominant market share in any individual P&C or reinsurance line, limiting pricing power
Mortgage segment earnings depend on U.S. housing/employment conditions and GSE policy, an external structural risk
Combined ratios and margins are inherently cyclical and cannot be fully insulated from a softening reinsurance market
Reliant on third-party reinsurance brokers for placement in both Insurance and Reinsurance segments

growth_drivers: Reinsurance segment scale following record underwriting income and premium growth in 2025 (net premiums written ~$7.6B, 80.8% combined ratio)
U.S. MidCorp and Entertainment insurance business acquired from Allianz (closed Aug 2024) expanding middle-market and entertainment specialty franchise
Continued Insurance segment growth (net premiums written +13% in 2025) as newly acquired books mature and cross-sell
Mortgage segment stability and capital efficiency via quota-share reinsurance/QRTCs, expected to lower reinsurance segment expense ratio to 3.9%-4.5% in 2026
Aggressive capital return via share repurchases ($1.2B in Q2 2026 alone) supporting per-share book value and EPS growth
Opportunistic capital redeployment across segments as pricing cycles diverge (casualty firming while property cat softens)
Rising investment income on a larger, higher-yielding fixed income portfolio versus the prior low-rate era

business.description: Property cat and specialty reinsurance exposure to hurricanes, earthquakes, wildfires and geopolitical events (e.g., Q2 2026 Insurance segment losses tied to the Iran conflict) can cause large single-quarter swings
Casualty and liability reserves face pressure from social inflation, nuclear jury verdicts, and third-party litigation funding, which could require adverse reserve development

business.risk: Softening reinsurance and property-cat pricing cycle
business.description: 2026 renewals saw property-cat rate-on-line declines of up to 25% at mid-year, the steepest since the late 1990s soft market, pressuring future underwriting margins
Six-player private MI market plus FHA competition is pressuring pricing/market share even as NIW volumes grow

financial.risk: Investment portfolio mark-to-market and credit risk
financial.description: Large fixed-income portfolio is sensitive to interest rate moves and credit spread widening
Global reinsurance business creates modest non-USD exposure, though Arch reports predominantly in USD

regulatory.description: Changes to Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac's role, PMIERs capital requirements, or increased GSE use of credit risk transfer (CRT) could materially affect the Mortgage segment's volumes and returns
As a Bermuda-domiciled group with global operations, Arch is exposed to evolving international tax rules (e.g., Pillar Two) and insurance capital regulation

regulatory.risk: State insurance regulation and rate approval
regulatory.description: U.S. admitted insurance lines require state rate/form approvals that can lag loss cost trends

macro.description: A recession or housing market deterioration would increase mortgage insurance claims and depress NIW volumes
Affects both investment income and mortgage origination volumes (refinance activity), a key driver of NIW
Rising frequency and severity of weather events could outpace catastrophe models and reinsurance pricing assumptions over time

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global reinsurance capital is at record levels, driving a multi-year softening in property-catastrophe pricing (down double digits at 2026 renewals) even as casualty/liability pricing continues to firm on social inflation; specialty and mortgage insurance markets remain more stable
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - P&C and reinsurance segments are classic underwriting-cycle businesses; Mortgage segment is more housing/credit-cycle driven and less correlated with catastrophe cycles, providing some smoothing
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - higher rates lift net investment income on Arch's large fixed-income float, but also affect mortgage origination/refinance volumes and bond portfolio valuations
key_input_costs: Loss cost trend (medical, construction, legal/social inflation)

recent_developments.event: Q2 2026 results: net income available to common of $1.0B ($3.00/share) vs $1.2B prior year; operating EPS of $2.56 beat consensus of $2.48; combined ratio 83.5%; book value per share rose 2.8% QoQ to $68.04

Reinsurance segment delivered $410M underwriting income aided by light catastrophe losses; Mortgage segment delivered $220M underwriting income on a resilient U.S. economy; Insurance segment underwriting hurt by catastrophe losses tied to the Iran conflict
Aggressive capital return: $1.2 billion of share repurchases in the quarter as management found valuation attractive amid a softening pricing cycle

Global property-catastrophe reinsurance rates fell sharply (up to ~25% risk-adjusted at June 1 renewals), the steepest annual decline since the late 1990s, pressuring Reinsurance segment margins into 2026-2027

Private mortgage insurance NIW volumes rose across all six major U.S. MIs; Arch was among the top gainers (~20% YoY growth) even as MGIC retained the largest volume share and FHA continues to take share from private MI

Record year: total capital ~$26.9B, net premiums written $16.5B; Reinsurance segment record $1.6B underwriting income at an 80.8% combined ratio (240bp improvement YoY); Insurance segment net premiums written +13% on MidCorp/Entertainment book

Closed $450M cash acquisition of Allianz's U.S. MidCorp and Entertainment insurance businesses (~$1.7B 2023 GPW), expanding U.S. middle-market and entertainment specialty franchise; ~500 former Allianz employees joined Arch

Announced CEO succession: Nicolas Papadopoulo (previously President & Chief Underwriting Officer) became CEO immediately, succeeding Marc Grandisson, who moved to Executive Chairman after leading Arch since 2018

items.metric: Catastrophe losses (as % of net earned premium)
items.notes: Full-year planning assumption embedded in segment loss ratio guidance
Benefiting from quota-share retrocession structures (QRTCs) that reduce the segment expense ratio
Company-level overhead guidance provided alongside segment targets
Management said it has no specific buyback target but found the stock attractive in Q2 2026, repurchasing $1.2B; capacity remains for further buybacks with wind-season risk in mind

guidance.management_commentary: Management described a 'cautious but opportunistic' stance as the market cycle enters an early softening phase, particularly in property catastrophe reinsurance pricing. They emphasized continued underwriting discipline and willingness to shrink volume in underpriced lines while redeploying capital toward buybacks and better-priced niches (e.g., casualty, mortgage). The Reinsurance and Mortgage segments were highlighted as sources of strength, while the Insurance segment absorbed elevated catastrophe losses (including Iran-conflict-related claims) in Q2 2026.

bull_case: Three-segment diversification (Insurance, Reinsurance, Mortgage) lets management rotate capital toward the best risk-adjusted returns through the cycle, a proven long-term strategy under both the outgoing and incoming CEO
Record Reinsurance segment profitability (80.8% combined ratio in 2025) and a stable, high-margin Mortgage segment provide an earnings floor even as property-cat pricing softens
Aggressive, consistent share buybacks ($1.2B in a single quarter) directly compound book value per share, which grew 4.5% in H1 2026
MidCorp/Entertainment acquisition adds a durable specialty middle-market franchise and diversifies the Insurance segment's mix
Elevated fixed-income yields versus the prior decade boost net investment income on Arch's large float
bear_case: Property-catastrophe reinsurance pricing is falling sharply (double-digit rate-on-line declines at 2026 renewals), the steepest since the late 1990s, which will compress Reinsurance segment margins in coming renewal cycles
Casualty reserve risk from social inflation and nuclear verdicts could force adverse reserve development across the industry, including Arch's casualty and professional lines books
Mortgage segment earnings are structurally exposed to U.S. housing/employment cycles and GSE/FHFA policy changes (PMIERs, increased CRT usage) that are outside Arch's control
No dominant share in any single line limits pricing power versus mega-reinsurers (Berkshire, Munich Re, Swiss Re), keeping Arch a price-taker in soft markets
CEO transition (Papadopoulo succeeding long-tenured Grandisson) introduces execution/continuity risk even though it was an internal, well-telegraphed succession
